title: Heal us
hook: names of the sick are added here in many communities

segments.voice: Yesterday, oni, the request to be seen in trouble. Your line was I hear you. Today, the eighth blessing, where people bring names.

Stand near someone saying the silent Amidah and, at one point, you might catch a pause, longer than usual. Their lips keep moving, but not with the printed words. If you could hear, you'd hear names. Sarah, daughter of Miriam. David, son of Ruth. A grandmother in the hospital. A friend's child in chemo. A coworker they barely know. The prayer book leaves a door open here, right in the middle of the prayer's fixed words.
screen: `A LONGER PAUSE.` → `NAMES, NOT PRINTED WORDS.` → `A DOOR LEFT OPEN.`

segments.voice: The eighth blessing begins with a verse from the prophet Jeremiah, who prays, in the old Jewish translation: "Heal me, O LORD, and I shall be healed; save me, and I shall be saved; for Thou art my praise." The Amidah changes one thing. Me becomes us. Heal us, and we shall be healed. Even about illness, the prayer speaks as a group. Then it asks for refuah shleimah, complete healing, for all our wounds, and ends: blessed are You, who heals the sick of Your people Israel. Refuah is healing; a rofe is a doctor, and you heard the same root in Gevurot: God heals the sick. The Talmud, in Megillah 17b, explains why healing is eighth: circumcision happens on the eighth day, and the baby needs healing after it. And in Avodah Zarah 8a, it says that a person with someone sick at home may mention them in this blessing. So in many communities, people add names here, quietly. A common custom is to use the person's Hebrew name and their mother's name: David son of Ruth. Some say the phrase refuah shleimah, complete healing, of body and of spirit. Notice the order of the requests: understanding, return, forgiveness, being seen, then healing. The body gets its turn right after the heart, and it gets it every day.
screen: `JEREMIAH: HEAL ME.` · `THE AMIDAH: HEAL US.` · `REFUAH SHLEIMAH: COMPLETE HEALING.` · `NAMES ADDED, WITH A MOTHER'S NAME.` · then, large: `HEAL US.`

segments.voice: Hold in mind someone who's sick right now, in body or in spirit, someone close or someone you only heard about, and say their name quietly; if you know their mother's name, you can add it, the way many Jews do. If you pray, you can ask for their complete healing. If not, simply hold the name with care for a few breaths.
Refuah. Healing. The Amidah's eighth blessing, Jeremiah's prayer made plural, where names of the sick are added.
Your line: thinking of you. The door in the prayer stays open every day. Five hundred eighty-five days now.
